question.worked_solution:
Let $u={log}_{8}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡8}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡8\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $8$ | $64$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $2$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{8}^{64}\frac{1}{x\sqrt{{log}_{8}⁡x}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{8}^{64}\frac{1}{\sqrt{{log}_{8}⁡x}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡8\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡8{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡8(2\sqrt{u}){|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡8(\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{1}) \\  & =2(\sqrt{2}-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡8\end{aligned}
$$
